'''Paul Dryden Warfield''' (born November 28, 1942) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 1964 to 1977 for the [[Cleveland Browns]] and [[Miami Dolphins]], except for a year in the [[World Football League]] (WFL) with the [[Memphis Southmen]] in 1975. He was known for his speed, fluid moves, grace, and jumping ability. A consistent big-play threat throughout his career, his 20.1 average yards per reception is the highest in NFL history among players with at least 300 receptions.

As a star [[Halfback (American football)|halfback]] playing [[college football]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]], Warfield was twice named to the [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|all-conference team]] in the [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]]. An [[All-America college football team|All-American]] as a senior, he was selected in the first round of the [[1964 NFL draft]] by the Browns and converted into a wide receiver. After three [[Pro Bowl]] appearances with the Browns, he was traded to the Dolphins, with whom he made another five Pro Bowl appearances. He then spent one season in the WFL with the Southmen before returning to the Browns for his final two seasons of play.

Warfield played in seven championship games in his professional career—four [[History of the NFL championship#NFL Championship Game (1933–1965)|NFL Championship Games]] with the Browns and three [[Super Bowl]]s with the Dolphins—and earned victories in the [[1964 NFL Championship Game]], [[Super Bowl VII]], and [[Super Bowl VIII]]. After his playing career, he served as a scout and adviser for the Browns for several years. He was inducted into the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 1983, and is a member of the [[Cleveland Browns#Ring of Honor|Cleveland Browns Ring of Honor]] and the [[Miami Dolphins Honor Roll]].

'''William Percy Harvin III''' (born May 28, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Florida Gators football|Florida Gators]], who won the [[BCS National Championship]] in 2006 and 2008. A two-time first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]], he was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the first round of the [[2009 NFL draft]]. Harvin also played for the [[Seattle Seahawks]], [[New York Jets]] and [[Buffalo Bills]]. He was named the [[National Football League Rookie of the Year Award|Associated Press Offensive Rookie of the Year]] in 2009 and won [[Super Bowl XLVIII]] with the Seahawks in 2013 over the [[Denver Broncos]]. He attended and played football for [[Landstown High School]] in [[Virginia Beach]], where his team won the high school state championship in 2004.

'''Percy Lee Snow''' (born November 5, 1967) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State Spartans]] from 1986 to 1989. As a senior, he was a consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] and won both the [[Butkus Award]] and the [[Lombardi Award]].
